statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). NQ trades at 29,384.25, down 65.25 points or 0.22%, after marking a marginal new low at 29,308.50 and then recovering about 76 points from it. ES has lifted off its own 7,663.00 low to 7,674.00. The extreme-holding, repeated-extension structure that lifted Tail to 24 last hour has resolved into a working retracement, so Tail eases to 20 and Stress to 71, while the broken 29,426.75 floor remains unreclaimed ahead of the European cash open.
recommendation: Tail at 20 sits at the bottom of the watch band, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The four-point decline from 24 records the loss of the specific evidence that produced it: NQ is no longer pinned to its session extreme, it has retraced roughly 40% of the Globex range from the low, and ES has done the same independently. Under this framework a functioning retracement is direct evidence against the pathological no-retracement path, and the overlay allows Tail to fall quickly once price discovery turns orderly. The score does not fall into the green band because the 29,426.75 floor that broke overnight has not been reclaimed, the European cash open is minutes away and is the first liquid test of that level, and the rate and energy backdrop is unchanged with the 10-year at 5.02%, the 30-year at 5.38% and WTI up 1.87% at 103.28. Stress remains high at 71 on that backdrop and on the two-day Federal Reserve meeting that opens today. The declared danger window is unchanged at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC around the US cash open, which remains the decisive test. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: NQ retraces about 76 points from a marginal 29,308.50 low to 29,384.25 with ES off its own low, resolving the extreme-holding structure - Tail eases from 24 to 20 with Stress high at 71
body: The development of this hour is the retracement, and it is the direct counterpart of last hour's failure. NQ extended marginally to a new session low at 29,308.50, six and a half points below the prior 29,315.00, and then recovered roughly 76 points to trade at 29,384.25, down 65.25 points or 0.22%. A second independent source shows the same structure, with the December contract at 29,386.50 against a 29,449.50 prior close. ES moved in parallel rather than diverging, lifting from its 7,663.00 low to 7,674.00, down 0.24%. The two conditions that took Tail from 17 to 24 an hour ago were repeated extension after a failed retracement and both US index futures pinned to their session extremes. Neither now holds. A recovery of about 40% of the Globex range from the low is the kind of two-way behaviour that a reverse or grid approach depends on, and the private framework applied here treats an observed working retracement as evidence against the no-retracement path rather than as a pause within it. That is why the score moves four points rather than drifting one. The case for keeping the score in the watch band rather than the green band is equally concrete. The 29,426.75 floor that broke during the 04:00 UTC hour has not been reclaimed; at 29,384.25 price is still 42.50 points below it, so what has happened is a retracement within a broken structure, not a repair of it. The European cash open at 07:00 UTC is minutes away and is the first genuinely liquid test of that level, and the same clock-hour band produced Monday's chip-led leg. The cross-asset backdrop is essentially unchanged: the 10-year is 5.02%, up 3.1 basis points and at its highest since 2007 on Trading Economics data, the 30-year is 5.38%, the 2-year is 4.68%, WTI is 103.28 up 1.87% and Brent 107.56 up 1.78% with the Saudi East-West pipeline still shut after drone strikes and reported to need weeks of repair, and VIX last closed at 17.10, up 7.95%. A two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today with the decision, projections and press conference on Wednesday. The regional evidence supports the retracement reading rather than contradicting it. The KOSPI recouped an early decline of almost 1% to trade up 0.15% at 6,694.11, with Samsung up 0.70% and SK Hynix up 1.27%, after a 3.26% drop on Monday; the quoted rationale was that the prior session had already priced the pressure from high US yields and the US chip slump. Monday's cash Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, having itself recovered 259.5 points from a 28,867.67 low. The honest reading is that the acute structural signal has cleared while the environment that produced it has not, which places the score at the bottom of the watch band. The conditional path treats the European cash open as the first checkpoint, the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases as a minor impulse window, the US cash open inside the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window as the decisive test, and the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC as a separate rates checkpoint given where the long end trades. None of these outcomes is observed at the assessment cutoff and the forecast states each as a checkpoint rather than as a resolved event. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read for this run but its collection timestamp is 01:00 UTC, more than five hours old and outside the freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and the assessment rests on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail entered the window at 19, rose through the European handover to 23, peaked at 26 during the European mid-morning chip-led decline and printed 25 in the following hour, eased through midday, reached 26 again at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon and evening to a 14 to 16 plateau across the overnight hours as Monday's decline was partly recovered. The final two slots lifted sharply, to 17 on the first break of the overnight floor and to 24 when that break was extended rather than reclaimed. Stress fell from a 79 peak to a 65 to 66 plateau before turning back up to 74 in the closing slot, and Confidence held between 86 and 89 throughout. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all tied to Monday's chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds 20 for the remainder of the pre-European hour, lifts to 23 for the European cash open at 07:00 UTC and holds 23 across the European mid-morning window that produced Monday's chip-led leg. It eases to 22, 21 and 20 through the European late morning and the pre-US lull, returns to 21 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and rises to 24 and then a 25 peak across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It eases to 22 and 21 through the US midday, lifts to 23 for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, holds 22 and 21 through the post-auction reaction and the power-hour approach, and falls to 20 at the cash close. It drops to 17 inside the futures maintenance halt, recovers to 18 at the Globex reopen, returns to 19 across the Tokyo open and the Asian mid-session on Federal Reserve decision day, eases to 18 through the Asian afternoon and the European handover, and closes the horizon at 19 into the European mid-morning ahead of the 12:30 UTC retail sales release and the 18:00 UTC decision. Every forecast value is conditional risk derived from scheduled checkpoints and the currently observed structure, not an assertion that any future price path has already been observed.
